identity.name: RMC SWITCHGEARS LIMITED
identity.industry: LT power-distribution hardware & utility EPC (electrical enclosures + solar/transmission EPC), pivoting to IoT grid-monitoring

summary.oneLiner: RMC Switchgears Limited is an electrical infrastructure company evolving into a technology-led provider for India's power distribution network, founder-led from Jaipur since 1994.
summary.business: RMC manufactures, distributes and sells power-distribution and safety products - smart-meter enclosures, feeder pillars, distribution and junction boxes, FRP safety products, panels and bus bars - and executes turnkey projects through Electrical EPC (transmission, distribution, substation automation and underground cabling) and Solar EPC (ground-mounted, rooftop and solar pumps). Products give it a manufacturing base, deep utility pre-qualifications and margin, while EPC turns those products into turnkey delivery and larger, bundled wins. It supplies state utilities, DISCOMs, PSUs and EPC …

Electrical Products: FRP safety products - V-cross arms, gratings, cable trays, transformer fencing
Electrical EPC: Smart-grid modernisation and SCADA-based substation monitoring and automation
Emerging technology platform: PulseBox - IS 14772-certified smart LT distribution box, an indigenous IoT platform for monitoring, verification and fault protection

currentContext.business: RMC manufactures, distributes and sells power-distribution and safety products - smart-meter enclosures, feeder pillars, distribution and junction boxes, FRP safety products, panels and bus bars - and executes turnkey projects through Electrical EPC (transmission, distribution, substation automation and underground cabling) and Solar EPC (ground-mounted, rooftop and solar pumps). plants.role: Sole anchor manufacturing site, established 2008; compounding, precision moulding, pultrusion, metal fabrication and mould and die making all on one site, so a design change can be made, tooled and validated without leaving the Company. A dedicated PulseBox line is being established here using in-house manufacturing and selective outsourcing.
plants.capacity: Site of roughly 90,000 sq. metres within a total manufacturing footprint of about 8,00,000 sq. ft. (grown from the first 5,000 sq. ft. unit and 35,000 sq. ft. by 2005); smart-meter enclosure capacity of about 3 lakh units a year; sheet moulding compound capacity scaling towards 15,000 MT a year

currentContext.strengths: Vertically integrated single site: compounding, precision moulding, pultrusion, metal fabrication and mould and die making at Chaksu, letting the Company design a part for a utility's field problem and be in production without waiting on an outside tool room - the sequence that produced both the multi-meter box for high-loss areas of Maharashtra and PulseBox|Materials capability as the enabler of certification: in-house sheet moulding compound gives the mechanical strength and dimensional stability utility enclosures need outdoors, and pultruded fibre-reinforced plastic gives non-conductive sections - a metal LT distribution box cannot be certified to IS 14772 because the conductivity is the hazard, whereas an FRP one can|Certification as the commercial barrier: a certified product transfers the utility's statutory liability at the low-tension layer to the standard; certification takes years and cannot be bought in, and management states no comparable certified product is in the field|Three decades of utility pre-qualifications and relationships behind an integrated product-plus-EPC model, where products supply the manufacturing base, pre-qualifications and margin, and EPC converts them into larger, bundled wins|Newly earned transmission pre-qualification - two letters of intent from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited for 132 kV grid sub-stations opened bidding for work that was closed to the Company a year earlier|MSEDCL as a marquee reference, with distribution infrastructure work in the Jalna and Satara circles serving as the template for utility-by-utility expansion; active discussions with five utilities and a PulseBox proof of concept deployed across five-plus states|ERP-led manufacturing flow with digitised quality-assurance documentation, which has reduced rework as volumes have grown|Migrated to the Main Board of the NSE and BSE in April 2026 after a 2017 BSE SME listing, and Forbes Asia Best Under a Billion recognition in 2025
currentContext.strategies: Run the established products-and-EPC business - Electrical Products, Electrical EPC and Solar EPC - selectively for quality and cash, and use it to fund an IP-led technology and manufacturing platform led by PulseBox, with both sharing the same plant, utility relationships and engineering base.|Quality of business over turnover - explicitly prioritise the bottom line and cash flows over top-line growth, with tighter working-capital discipline, prudent capital allocation, improved return on investment and a return to positive operating cash flow and a stronger balance sheet in FY2027.|Centrally funded project focus and utility selectivity - favour centrally funded and centrally sponsored work such as RDSS distribution projects where funding and payment discipline are stronger, and be deliberate about which state utilities to take on.|MOAT-focused project selection - take work in transmission lines, substations and underground cabling alongside smart-grid modernisation and SCADA-based substation monitoring and automation, because each selective win earns the pre-qualifications that gate entry to bigger tenders.|Product-range transition up the voltage curve - move Electrical Products from low-voltage toward medium- and high-voltage panels over about 18 to 24 months to serve underground cabling, transmission lines, data centres, EV charging, solar parks, thermal plants and battery storage.|Utility-by-utility expansion - prove the model end-to-end at MSEDCL (Jalna and Satara circles) and extend it, with active discussions with five utilities and a PulseBox proof of concept deployed across five-plus states.|Price risk explicitly: every significant EPC bid now carries price-escalation provisions, procurement is planned on longer lead times, and the Company will decline work priced on the assumption that nothing goes wrong.|Size capital to demonstrated evidence - the PulseBox line is sized to what ten pilot installations have demonstrated, not to the scale of the addressable market, so that if demand arrives more slowly the Company has not committed capital against a forecast.|PulseBox will be made in India and the Company intends to control the intellectual property, with the structure of that holding being finalised with legal and governance input.|Direct research work at the problems utilities raise and at the low-tension layer, currently monitoring of harmonics and power factor as variable-quality domestic electric vehicle chargers connect to low-tension networks, and preventive maintenance scheduling for utilities that currently operate reactively.
currentContext.expansion: This bundle carries no plant, capacity or capital-expenditure disclosure for RMC itself; the expansion visible in it is expansion of the order footprint and of the corporate structure. In transmission, the Company held no pre-qualification until FY2026 and then received two letters of intent in November 2025 from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, of Rs 27.78 crore and Rs 42.24 crore, for 132 kV grid sub-stations at Kaparda SEZ in Jodhpur and at Kalyanpur, Balotra, with associated lines and bays; both are supply, erection, testing and commissioning contracts over eighteen months with billing from the second quarter of FY2027, and management states the value matters less than the credential because it can now bid for work that was closed to it a year ago. In distribution, FY2026 was the year the opportunity was converted into signed work, with Rs 59.12 crore secured from Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited for segregation of 11 kV mixed feeders at Tonk Circle followed by Rs 84.38 crore for the same work at Jhalawar Circle, and phase two of the scheme expected to extend investment further into low-tension infrastructure, where the next product generation is directed. In solar, an 8.8 MWac installation was completed for the Maharashtra State Power Generation Company in December 2025, with the order book at about Rs 125 crore and active tenders of about Rs 400 crore. On the technology platform, PulseBox - India's first smart LT distribution box certified to IS 14772 and type tested by the Central Power Research Institute - closed FY2026 live on ten pilot distribution transformers across five states, with three states in advanced commercial discussion, no pilot discontinued, and no revenue and no date placed on the first order. Structurally, the Company has built out a subsidiary stack for the solar and green-energy business - RMC Green Energy Private Limited (incorporated 15th July 2024), RMC Solar Park Private Limited (19th September 2024), RMC Solar One Private Limited (26th March 2026), RMC Solar Two Private Limited (5th June 2025), RMC Solar Three Private Limited (30th May 2025) and RMC Solar Five Private Limited (30th May 2025) - with RMC Solar Park Private Limited becoming a material subsidiary on the significant growth in its business operations, and a loan of Rs 1,034.43 lakh granted during the year to RMC Green Energy Private Limited under Section 186. To fund what follows, the Board has recommended raising Authorised Share Capital from Rs 15,00,00,000 to Rs 20,00,00,000, expressly to support future growth plans, strategic expansion initiatives and flexibility for future fund-raising, issuance of securities and employee stock options.
currentContext.mdna: Distribution modernisation under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (outlay about Rs 3.03 lakh crore, around Rs 2.8 lakh crore of projects approved), targeting aggregate technical and commercial losses of 12% to 15%; distribution is where most of RMC's product range lives.|DISCOM financial health as the demand precondition - losses fell from 22.62% in FY2014 to 15.04% in FY2025 and distribution utilities posted a profit of Rs 2,701 crore in FY2025 against losses of Rs 67,962 crore in FY2014; management calls a distribution sector that makes money the figure that matters most to it.|Smart-metering runway - 5.72 crore smart meters installed, 4.05 crore of them under RDSS, leaving a multi-year runway that drives demand for meter enclosures, feeder pillars and distribution boxes.|Transmission build-out - the National Electricity Plan commits an estimated Rs 9.15 lakh crore between 2023 and 2032, expanding the network from about five lakh to 6.48 lakh circuit kilometres and transformation capacity from 1,407 GVA to 2,345 GVA toward a 458 GW peak demand; RMC only earned transmission pre-qualification in FY2026.|Renewable execution - renewable capacity reached 258.01 GW by December 2025 within total installed capacity of 513.79 GW, with India working toward 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 including 280 GW of solar; demand is not the constraint in solar, margin discipline is.|The uncertified low-tension layer as a market RMC is attempting to create rather than compete in - around 2.5 crore distribution transformers in India, roughly 75 lakh assessed as realistically addressable and the underlying problem sized at over Rs 50,000 crore; PulseBox carried no revenue in FY2026 and management will not put a date on the first order.|Mix rotation in FY2026 - Solar EPC became the largest vertical at Rs 208.99 crore (about 52%), Electrical EPC reset to Rs 96.13 crore from Rs 253.72 crore after extended rainfall in Maharashtra and procurement challenges, and Electrical Products grew about 59% to Rs 96.48 crore.|Blended margins lifted by certified, intelligent products, with Electrical Products outlook anchored on smart metering, distribution upgrades and RDSS incentives plus a path into MV and HV panels, LV retail and smart-meter-enclosure scale-up.|Margin headwinds management frames as addressable rather than continuing - input-cost inflation in steel, copper, aluminium and silver, year-end fuel, freight and logistics pressure, China-linked supply-chain disruption and safeguard-duty movements in solar, execution delays, cost absorption on older fixed-price orders, and expensed PulseBox development; the response is better project selection, stronger procurement discipline, improved execution oversight and prudent capital allocation.|Second-half shape of the year is the evidence management points to - a loss of Rs 7.07 crore in Q3 followed by a profit of Rs 9.30 crore in Q4 on better execution, improved material availability, project catch-up, a stronger project mix and tighter operating discipline.|Confirmed order book exceeded Rs 800 crore at year-end, providing visibility into execution in FY2027.|Active tenders exceeded Rs 1,500 crore - opportunities the Company is bidding for, not confirmed orders.|Within the confirmed book, disclosed components are the Solar EPC order book of about Rs 125 crore, the first Transmission EPC order of about Rs 70 crore and Electrical Products execution of about Rs 35 crore, with the remainder spread across Electrical EPC and other work.|Within tenders, disclosed components are about Rs 400 crore in Solar EPC and an Rs 89 crore Electrical Products pipeline, with the balance across other verticals.|Distribution wins in FY2026: Rs 59.12 crore from Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited for segregation of 11 kV mixed feeders at Tonk Circle, followed by Rs 84.38 crore for the same work at Jhalawar Circle.|Transmission entry: two letters of intent in November 2025 from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, of Rs 27.78 crore and Rs 42.24 crore, for 132 kV grid sub-stations at Kaparda SEZ in Jodhpur and at Kalyanpur, Balotra, with associated lines and bays - supply, erection, testing and commissioning over eighteen months with billing from the second quarter of FY2027. Management says the value matters less than the credential.

risks.note: Copper, aluminium, electrical-grade steel and polymer-linked materials remained high through FY2026 and the rupee weakened by roughly 9% against the US dollar, raising the landed cost of imported inputs; gross margin moved from 29.68% to 23.67%. Mitigation is price-escalation clauses in EPC bids, selective bidding and disciplined procurement.

risks.risk: Fixed-price contract exposure on work already in execution
risks.note: Several contracts in execution had been priced without escalation provisions, so cost increases were absorbed by the Company rather than shared with customers. Escalation-linked pricing applies only to bids submitted since the third quarter of FY2026; contracts already in execution run off through FY2027.

EPC work ties up working capital in receivables and retention, and operating cash flow turned negative in FY2026 under debtor and retention pressure. Mitigation is a focus on centrally funded, payment-disciplined utilities and tighter working-capital management, with a stated aim of positive operating cash flow and a stronger balance sheet in FY2027.
Site conditions, weather and long pipeline-to-order cycles can delay revenue. Mitigation is stronger execution oversight, selective project intake and seasonality planning.

risks.risk: Technology and adoption risk on PulseBox
risks.note: PulseBox is early and utility adoption is unproven at scale; development expenditure on it continued through the year, concentrated in the third quarter. Mitigation is pilot-led validation, national certification and a phased transition from proof of concept to commercial scale.

Red Sea and China-linked disruptions together with safeguard-duty movements extended procurement cycles by nearly two months in some cases, and from around December movements in aluminium and silver and the withdrawal of Chinese module subsidies raised module costs in the largest vertical.

risks.risk: Concentration in a single plant and in solar execution
risks.note: Manufacturing is anchored by the single Chaksu plant of roughly 8,00,000 sq. ft., while Solar EPC became the largest vertical at Rs 208.99 crore and carried most of the year's input-cost exposure. A confirmed order book above Rs 800 crore concentrates FY2027 delivery in that same execution capability.

one-line thesis: A small-cap Rajasthan electrical-infra contractor (enclosures + solar/T&D EPC) trying to re-rate from a low-margin "red-ocean" EPC player into a tech-led utility solutions company via PulseBox, an IoT LT-line/transformer monitoring device — but FY26 exposed serious working-capital and execution fragility, and the stock is down >75% from its top.

guidance (next quarter / fy27):
- **No formal FY27 revenue/PAT guidance** ("speaking very early this year"; will not give numbers). VERIFY against any later quarterly call.
- Qualitative: "we'll do better than last year, that is for sure"; explicitly shifting from growth-at-any-cost to project selection on bottom-line + cash flow, with bigger execution buffers.
- H1 FY27 flagged as the period when most retention money should be realised → positive cash flow expected in FY27.
- Long-term aspiration reaffirmed: ₹5,000 cr "by FY30" (~10x, framed as aspiration, not guidance).
order book & pipeline:
- Unexecuted order book ₹850 cr+; tender pipeline ₹1,500 cr+ (both comprehensive across segments).
- Execution timelines: electrical EPC ~2 yrs, solar EPC ~1 yr, products ~3 months — plus added buffer post-FY26 lessons.
- No segment split of order book provided on call (CEO to email; data not available live — watch-item).
- Andhra Pradesh green-corridor tenders awaited (delayed, pending central approval).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- Four operating thrusts: electrical products, electrical EPC, solar EPC, PulseBox.
- Revenue mix heavily B2G: solar EPC and electrical EPC are ~100% government; within electrical products ~30% govt / 70% B2B. Net company-level B2B only ~5–10%.
- IHSPL subsidiary sold; water conservation/treatment vertical (in prior deck) explicitly dropped — refocusing on energy only.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **PulseBox** (core optionality): IoT LT-distribution monitor — real-time current cut-off on fault, theft/electrocution prevention, transformer protection (overload/under-voltage/thermal), power-quality/harmonics monitoring (incl. EV-charger pollution). POC done; pilot in one state gave 388 alarms in 7 days, utility replaced a transformer pre-failure; one utility moved to spec/tender drafting. Claimed sole player ("we are the only one"). TAM framing: 2.5 cr DTs → ~75 lakh addressable urban/high-theft → ₹50,000 cr+ at only ~15–20% price premium over traditional boxes. Explicitly "not guidance / not an order book."
- MV/HV panel expansion under feasibility study (sell to solar plants, thermal plants, data centres, EV chargers).
- Retail/organised-enclosure play (HR-led, low capex).
- Next R&D project started post-PulseBox (undisclosed); "strategic collaboration" partner undisclosed (trade secret); tech from Western partners, "made in India."
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 margins hit by: PulseBox product-dev investment, project execution delays, input-cost inflation (aluminium, silver, steel, copper, polymer, sheet metal; WPI 3.88% Mar-2026; fuel/freight/logistics).
- Solar EPC specifically squeezed: China supply-chain disruption + safeguard duty + higher module input costs forced cancel/rework/defer of older fixed-price orders; procurement lead times +~2 months.
- Q4 recovery via tighter cost control, better material availability, stronger project mix/conversion.
capex / expansion:
- No major capex announced; MV/HV and retail expansion described as HR-led rather than capex-heavy.
- R&D spend to remain elevated as a strategic priority.
capital allocation:
- Stated pivot to "prudent capital allocation to increase ROI YoY"; project selection on bottom-line + cash flow over top line; working-capital discipline; stronger balance sheet targeted in FY27.
- Promoter (Agarwal family) buying: CEO hinted "you might see in coming months" — unconfirmed.
risks & watch-items:
- **Working capital / cash flow**: receivables ₹148→₹205 cr, negative CFO — recovery is the swing factor; only 3–5% claimed >6 months (ex-retention), exact aging not provided.
- **B2G concentration** (~90%+ govt) → no fixed payment due-dates, "WIP invoice" risk, billing-process dependency on officers.
- **Fixed-price EPC vs input volatility** — already caused FY26 order cancellations/reworks.
- **PulseBox = pre-revenue optionality**: zero confirmed orders; long utility tender cycles; TAM is aspirational.
- **Credibility/governance optics**: stock −75% from top; ₹5,000 cr-by-FY30 aspiration vs ₹400 cr base is very aggressive; selective disclosure (declined order-book split, collaboration name, segment B2B/B2G specifics live).
management quality / tone:
- Single-executive call (CEO only) — promotional, aspiration-heavy, vague on hard numbers; repeatedly deflected requests for splits/guidance ("email me," "trade secret," "can't disclose").
- Candid on FY26 being a "learning year" and on cash-flow stress, which is a positive. But heavy reliance on TAM storytelling (PulseBox ₹50,000 cr) against a tiny revenue base and a collapsed stock warrants skepticism. Tone: earnest but salesman-ish.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The real FY26 story is balance-sheet stress (receivables + negative CFO), not the headline +26% revenue — and the +26% was largely low-quality, lumpy March-loaded govt billing.
- PulseBox is positioned in the gap smart meters can't fill: meters *detect* AT&C loss after ~30 days; PulseBox *acts* in real time (cuts current). If RDSS Phase-2 funds LT-layer monitoring, this is the genuine optionality — but it is a single-product, single-pilot bet today.
- EV-charger proliferation is framed as a demand driver (harmonic/power-quality pollution on LT line that PulseBox monitors) — an indirect EV linkage, not direct EV supply.
- Water-management vertical and IHSPL both exited — narrative is narrowing to "energy/electrical only," a sensible de-cluttering.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: RMC Switchgears Limited is an electrical infrastructure company evolving into a technology-led provider for India's power distribution network, founder-led from Jaipur since 1994.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: RMC manufactures, distributes and sells power-distribution and safety products - smart-meter enclosures, feeder pillars, distribution and junction boxes, FRP safety products, panels and bus bars - and executes turnkey projects through Electrical EPC (transmission, distribution, substation automation and underground cabling) and Solar EPC (ground-mounted, rooftop and solar pumps). Products give it a manufacturing base, deep utility pre-qualifications and margin, while EPC turns those products into turnkey delivery and larger, bundled wins. It supplies state utilities, DISCOMs, PSUs and EPC majors, and is building a fourth, IP-led platform around PulseBox, its certified smart LT distribution box, offering both hardware and software along with end-to-end installation and management services.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Distribution modernisation under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (outlay about Rs 3.03 lakh crore, around Rs 2.8 lakh crore of projects approved), targeting aggregate technical and commercial losses of 12% to 15%; distribution is where most of RMC's product range lives.
- DISCOM financial health as the demand precondition - losses fell from 22.62% in FY2014 to 15.04% in FY2025 and distribution utilities posted a profit of Rs 2,701 crore in FY2025 against losses of Rs 67,962 crore in FY2014; management calls a distribution sector that makes money the figure that matters most to it.
- Smart-metering runway - 5.72 crore smart meters installed, 4.05 crore of them under RDSS, leaving a multi-year runway that drives demand for meter enclosures, feeder pillars and distribution boxes.
- Transmission build-out - the National Electricity Plan commits an estimated Rs 9.15 lakh crore between 2023 and 2032, expanding the network from about five lakh to 6.48 lakh circuit kilometres and transformation capacity from 1,407 GVA to 2,345 GVA toward a 458 GW peak demand; RMC only earned transmission pre-qualification in FY2026.
- Renewable execution - renewable capacity reached 258.01 GW by December 2025 within total installed capacity of 513.79 GW, with India working toward 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 including 280 GW of solar; demand is not the constraint in solar, margin discipline is.
- The uncertified low-tension layer as a market RMC is attempting to create rather than compete in - around 2.5 crore distribution transformers in India, roughly 75 lakh assessed as realistically addressable and the underlying problem sized at over Rs 50,000 crore; PulseBox carried no revenue in FY2026 and management will not put a date on the first order.
- Mix rotation in FY2026 - Solar EPC became the largest vertical at Rs 208.99 crore (about 52%), Electrical EPC reset to Rs 96.13 crore from Rs 253.72 crore after extended rainfall in Maharashtra and procurement challenges, and Electrical Products grew about 59% to Rs 96.48 crore.
- Blended margins lifted by certified, intelligent products, with Electrical Products outlook anchored on smart metering, distribution upgrades and RDSS incentives plus a path into MV and HV panels, LV retail and smart-meter-enclosure scale-up.
- Margin headwinds management frames as addressable rather than continuing - input-cost inflation in steel, copper, aluminium and silver, year-end fuel, freight and logistics pressure, China-linked supply-chain disruption and safeguard-duty movements in solar, execution delays, cost absorption on older fixed-price orders, and expensed PulseBox development; the response is better project selection, stronger procurement discipline, improved execution oversight and prudent capital allocation.
- Second-half shape of the year is the evidence management points to - a loss of Rs 7.07 crore in Q3 followed by a profit of Rs 9.30 crore in Q4 on better execution, improved material availability, project catch-up, a stronger project mix and tighter operating discipline.
- Confirmed order book exceeded Rs 800 crore at year-end, providing visibility into execution in FY2027.
- Active tenders exceeded Rs 1,500 crore - opportunities the Company is bidding for, not confirmed orders.
- Within the confirmed book, disclosed components are the Solar EPC order book of about Rs 125 crore, the first Transmission EPC order of about Rs 70 crore and Electrical Products execution of about Rs 35 crore, with the remainder spread across Electrical EPC and other work.
- Within tenders, disclosed components are about Rs 400 crore in Solar EPC and an Rs 89 crore Electrical Products pipeline, with the balance across other verticals.
- Distribution wins in FY2026: Rs 59.12 crore from Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited for segregation of 11 kV mixed feeders at Tonk Circle, followed by Rs 84.38 crore for the same work at Jhalawar Circle.
- Transmission entry: two letters of intent in November 2025 from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, of Rs 27.78 crore and Rs 42.24 crore, for 132 kV grid sub-stations at Kaparda SEZ in Jodhpur and at Kalyanpur, Balotra, with associated lines and bays - supply, erection, testing and commissioning over eighteen months with billing from the second quarter of FY2027. Management says the value matters less than the credential.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: This bundle carries no plant, capacity or capital-expenditure disclosure for RMC itself; the expansion visible in it is expansion of the order footprint and of the corporate structure. In transmission, the Company held no pre-qualification until FY2026 and then received two letters of intent in November 2025 from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, of Rs 27.78 crore and Rs 42.24 crore, for 132 kV grid sub-stations at Kaparda SEZ in Jodhpur and at Kalyanpur, Balotra, with associated lines and bays; both are supply, erection, testing and commissioning contracts over eighteen months with billing from the second quarter of FY2027, and management states the value matters less than the credential because it can now bid for work that was closed to it a year ago. In distribution, FY2026 was the year the opportunity was converted into signed work, with Rs 59.12 crore secured from Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited for segregation of 11 kV mixed feeders at Tonk Circle followed by Rs 84.38 crore for the same work at Jhalawar Circle, and phase two of the scheme expected to extend investment further into low-tension infrastructure, where the next product generation is directed. In solar, an 8.8 MWac installation was completed for the Maharashtra State Power Generation Company in December 2025, with the order book at about Rs 125 crore and active tenders of about Rs 400 crore. On the technology platform, PulseBox - India's first smart LT distribution box certified to IS 14772 and type tested by the Central Power Research Institute - closed FY2026 live on ten pilot distribution transformers across five states, with three states in advanced commercial discussion, no pilot discontinued, and no revenue and no date placed on the first order. Structurally, the Company has built out a subsidiary stack for the solar and green-energy business - RMC Green Energy Private Limited (incorporated 15th July 2024), RMC Solar Park Private Limited (19th September 2024), RMC Solar One Private Limited (26th March 2026), RMC Solar Two Private Limited (5th June 2025), RMC Solar Three Private Limited (30th May 2025) and RMC Solar Five Private Limited (30th May 2025) - with RMC Solar Park Private Limited becoming a material subsidiary on the significant growth in its business operations, and a loan of Rs 1,034.43 lakh granted during the year to RMC Green Energy Private Limited under Section 186. To fund what follows, the Board has recommended raising Authorised Share Capital from Rs 15,00,00,000 to Rs 20,00,00,000, expressly to support future growth plans, strategic expansion initiatives and flexibility for future fund-raising, issuance of securities and employee stock options.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated single site: compounding, precision moulding, pultrusion, metal fabrication and mould and die making at Chaksu, letting the Company design a part for a utility's field problem and be in production without waiting on an outside tool room - the sequence that produced both the multi-meter box for high-loss areas of Maharashtra and PulseBox
- Materials capability as the enabler of certification: in-house sheet moulding compound gives the mechanical strength and dimensional stability utility enclosures need outdoors, and pultruded fibre-reinforced plastic gives non-conductive sections - a metal LT distribution box cannot be certified to IS 14772 because the conductivity is the hazard, whereas an FRP one can
- Certification as the commercial barrier: a certified product transfers the utility's statutory liability at the low-tension layer to the standard; certification takes years and cannot be bought in, and management states no comparable certified product is in the field
- Three decades of utility pre-qualifications and relationships behind an integrated product-plus-EPC model, where products supply the manufacturing base, pre-qualifications and margin, and EPC converts them into larger, bundled wins
- Newly earned transmission pre-qualification - two letters of intent from Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited for 132 kV grid sub-stations opened bidding for work that was closed to the Company a year earlier
- MSEDCL as a marquee reference, with distribution infrastructure work in the Jalna and Satara circles serving as the template for utility-by-utility expansion; active discussions with five utilities and a PulseBox proof of concept deployed across five-plus states
- ERP-led manufacturing flow with digitised quality-assurance documentation, which has reduced rework as volumes have grown
- Migrated to the Main Board of the NSE and BSE in April 2026 after a 2017 BSE SME listing, and Forbes Asia Best Under a Billion recognition in 2025
